Quality partly; cost works. (2) AST: 0.757 / 755K; 50.6% / 2.45M; 45.3% / 1.77M; 25.3% / 656K; wall 105-209 s. Quality partly; cost works. (3) Callgraph: 0.770 / 683K; 46.2% / 2.31M; 37.9% / 1.69M; 34.3% / 614K; wall 105-201 s. Quality partly (best SecBench, worst SWT); cost works. (4) Deps: 0.757 / 628K; 49.4% / 2.41M; 42.9% / 1.77M; 31.9% / 651K; wall 88-205 s. Quality partly; cost works. (5) Docs: 0.770 / 663K; 44.3% / 2.53M; 47.2% / 1.82M; 31.3% / 698K; wall 106-290 s. Relative to baseline, wall time rises with all workflows on LinuxFL, SWT, SecBench (SecBench 66 s vs 136-290 s) and falls on SWE-Pro (269 s vs 194-209 s)

rev.why: The baseline entry had no quality or cost verdict (protocol §6). The cost verdicts were comparative ('works except SWT' because SWT tokens exceed the baseline), against the rule that each configuration is judged on its own; all six spend 0.61-3.12M tokens and 66-290 s per task with Haiku 4.5 (Tables III-VI, pp. 6-7), so the same verdict is given to all. 'Works' rather than 'partly' is a judgement: no money figure is reported. Values rechecked against Tables III-VI; per-configuration wall-time ranges added from the tables

fields.v: Grid: (1 baseline + 5 workflows) x 4 benchmarks, same sampled task IDs (deterministic seed). Held constant: agent (Claude Code), model and effort, built-in tools pinned, benchmark prompt; treatment adds MCP server plus representation-use steer (and on repair a map-first hook). Acceptance: benchmark hidden tests/harnesses. Repetitions: 1 per task per workflow (k=1). Human intervention: none

Fault localization: all workflows improve recall@10 (0.757-0.829 vs 0.717; Hybrid +15.6%) and cut tokens 25-39%, but increase wall time. Program repair: resolution ~baseline (44.3-50.6% vs 49.0%), tokens -17-26%, faster. Security patching: Callgraph best (34.3% vs 28.9%), mixed tokens, all slower. Test generation: Hybrid/Docs slightly better (47.8%, 47.2% vs 44.7%), all use more tokens and time. No significance tests; differences on SWT/SecBench treated as descriptive

Distinguished workflows mainly on localization and token cost; success differences on repair, test and security often within one-shot variance. Not repeated (k=1). Limitations stated: treatment confounds representation content with steering and map-first hook; single agent/model; metrics omit map-construction and human costs

Non-determinism of agent runs; treatment combines representation content, availability and map-first steering; one agent stack (Claude Code + Haiku 4.5) and four benchmarks; benchmark success does not capture patch quality or developer usefulness; token counts omit human and one-time infrastructure costs; k=1 runs, small differences may be variance. Out-of-map tasks (tree-wide replace, new files, config/YAML edits) defeat all maps. Recommends choosing representations by task bottleneck
